title: declare-compat-values-and-serial-init-controller-for-onprem-installs
author: Asha Patel
body:
Motivation:
This PR refactors the helm values surface for the private installer to make explicit a compatibility layer and to add a serial init controller pattern suitable for on-prem tenant bootstrap sequences. Over time we've accumulated ad-hoc values and a few implicit ordering assumptions in init jobs; that has made upgrades brittle for customers running large tenant counts.

What this changes (summary):
- Add a top-level `compat` values section that maps legacy keys to the new canonical schema and emits a Helm note when values are detected that will be deprecated.
- Introduce a `serial-init-controller` Kubernetes manifest (lightweight controller) as a templated init helper that enforces per-tenant serial execution of seed/init hooks. This is opt-in and controlled by values (`init.controller.enabled`).
- Strict values schema (values.schema.json) extended with `compat` rules and deprecation metadata; Helm lint and CI now fail if unknown top-level keys are present unless they are explicitly mapped in `compat`.
- Add a small Go utility (`scripts/values_migrate.go`) used in our release tooling to produce a migration plan for customer `values.yaml` during upgrades (dry-run and apply modes).
- Update Helm helpers (`_helpers.tpl`) with new template functions `compatMerge` and `initControllerConfig` used across the chart to maintain single source of truth.

Design and compatibility notes:
- The `compat` section allows chart operators to declare mapping from legacy keys to canonical keys, for example: `compat: { oldInitConcurrency: { to: init.controller.concurrency, warn: true } }`. When `warn` is true, Helm will render a NOTICE in the template output but will not break installs. A future major will promote `warn` -> error by default.
- `init.controller.enabled` defaults to `false` for backwards compatibility. We recommend enabling it for clusters upgrading to this chart if they have >50 concurrent tenant seeds.
- The serial controller is intentionally minimal (no external dependencies) and acts by creating a per-tenant Lease and running init Jobs sequentially; it's implemented as a templated Deployment for customers who prefer managed controller, and as a Job-driven fallback for air-gapped environments.

Checklist:
- [x] Add values.schema.json entries for new fields and deprecation metadata
- [x] Implement `compat` merging helpers in `_helpers.tpl`
- [x] Add `serial-init-controller` manifests + RBAC templates
- [x] Add `scripts/values_migrate.go` and CI task to run migration dry-runs in release pipeline
- [x] Document deprecation path in CHART_NOTES and docs/upgrade.md

Release and rollout plan:
1) Publish chart with this change in a minor release (no breaking behavior by default).
2) Encourage customers to run `values-migrate --dry-run` (bundled in the upgrade checklist) to see suggested translations.
3) After two minor releases, flip `compat.warn` -> `compat.strict` behavior in a major (breaking) bump.

Testing and CI:
- Unit tests added for template helper logic (helm unit harness) and small integration run in the CI that renders the chart against legacy example values/modern example values.
- The first CI run failed due to schema validation for multi-document notes; fixed by narrowing the schema pattern and re-running. Final CI status: pass.

Notes for reviewers:
- Focus on the `values.schema.json` deprecation metadata shape and whether the `compat` mapping covers the existing customer feature set (I added mappings observed in support tickets from ENG-9876).
- The serial controller is intentionally conservative in permissions; feedback welcome if we should widen RBAC for multi-namespace operators.

Related: ENG-9876 (tenant-seed-failures), ENG-10231 (upgrade-hardening)
commits: a1f4bd1  create compat values scaffold and values.schema additions
b67e2c3  add serial-init-controller templates and RBAC; wire template helpers
c9d8a7f  add scripts/values_migrate.go and CI dry-run integration; docs updates
review_comments: Marcus Velez: Can you confirm the controller's Lease duration defaults? If it's too short we risk collisions during slow preflight checks.
Asha Patel: Response: Increased default lease TTL to 60s and made it configurable at init.controller.leaseTTL. Added comment in RBAC template.
Elena Cho: The compat mapping is helpful, but we should add an automated smoke test that renders charts with historical values bundles (saw a mismatch for oldInitImagePullPolicy).
Asha Patel: Added a small legacy-values bundle in testdata and CI render job to cover that case.
Samir Gupta: Approval pending on RBAC scope — prefer Namespace-scoped by default. Consider making ClusterRole optional.
Asha Patel: Updated templates to default to Role/RoleBinding and only render ClusterRole when `.Values.init.controller.clusterScope` is true.
release_notes: Add compatibility layer for legacy values, opt-in serial init controller for tenant seed ordering, and migration tooling for values.yaml. No breaking changes by default.
